mainEntity.name: Does frame size change how much I should weigh?

acceptedAnswer.text: It's one factor some ideal-weight frameworks consider — a larger frame generally supports a somewhat higher healthy weight than a smaller frame at the same height, commonly by about 10% either way, though it's just one of many relevant factors.

mainEntity.name: Where exactly should I measure my wrist?

acceptedAnswer.text: At the narrowest point of the wrist, just below the wrist bone — roughly where a watch strap would sit — using a flexible tape measure snug against the skin.

mainEntity.name: Why do the two methods sometimes disagree?

acceptedAnswer.text: The ratio method scales smoothly with height, while the MedlinePlus chart uses broad height bands with fixed wrist ranges. Near a band edge they can land in neighbouring categories; if they differ, you're likely near the border between the two sizes.

mainEntity.name: What wrist size is a small, medium or large frame?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your sex and height. At 170 cm, a man is roughly small under 16.3 cm, medium to 17.7 cm and large above that; a woman is roughly small under 15.5 cm, medium to 16.8 cm and large above that. The calculator shows the exact bands for your own height.
Not meaningfully once you are fully grown. Weight, fat and muscle change, but your skeletal frame, and therefore your wrist measurement, stays close to the same.

mainEntity.name: Is frame size the same as body shape or body type?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Frame size is about skeletal build relative to height. Body shape is about how weight is distributed, and somatotypes such as ectomorph or endomorph are an older informal way of describing physique.
BMI only uses height and weight, so it does not adjust for frame size. Frame size is sometimes used as extra context when judging a weight range, but it does not change your BMI.

mainEntity.name: What if the ratio and the chart give different frame sizes?

acceptedAnswer.text: That usually means you are close to the border between two sizes. The ratio method changes smoothly with height while the chart uses fixed height bands, so near a band edge either label is reasonable.
